title: Animal Welfare Education and Ethical Perceptions Among Veterinary Students at Two Ecuadorian Universities
content: Animal welfare education should connect ethical concern with scientific understand-ing and practical judgement. This cross-sectional descriptive and comparative study ex-amined 369 veterinary students at Universidad Técnica de Manabí (UTM; n = 176) and Escuela Superior Politécnica Agropecuaria de Manabí Manuel Félix López (ESPAM MFL; n = 193), Ecuador. A structured questionnaire and 24 semistructured interviews explored educational experience and ethical perceptions. Frequencies and percentages described responses; institutional distributions were compared using appropriate categorical tests with Holm adjustment across 14 items. High self-reported 3Rs familiarity was reported by 58.0% at UTM and 22.8% at ESPAM MFL. Frequent receipt of Five Freedoms infor-mation was reported by 84.7% and 67.4%, respectively. Differences in these items, course-work exposure, perceived ethical influence on professional decisions, and exposure to spaces promoting the 3Rs remained after adjustment. Adjusted comparisons did not es-tablish institutional differences in facilities, participation or support for empathy assess-ment. Interview accounts highlighted useful learning and requests for greater practical experience. Findings describe reported experience rather than objective competence and cannot establish causal effects of educational programmes.
